cohort: The study included patients undergoing elective caesarean section, aged 20 to 60, and classified as ASA grade I or II.
finding: Fentanyl, when used as an adjunct to spinal bupivacaine in elective caesarean sections, significantly prolonged analgesia, motor block, and sensory block, and resulted in lower post-operative pain levels compared to tramadol, despite both providing adequate surgical anesthesia.
